closedPRs.title: parity:platform-spellcheck — on-device English spellcheck in the composer
closedPRs.body:
## What

On-device spellcheck in the message composer (README: `- [x] Spellcheck in composer`).

- **Engine** (`src/spellcheck.rs`, pure Rust, zero system deps): embedded frequency-ordered English wordlist (~48k words, `assets/spellcheck/en.txt`, from FrequencyWords en_50k); hash lookups for correctness; Damerau-Levenshtein distance-1 edits (capped distance-2 fallback) ranked by frequency for suggestions. Only ASCII words are checked — other scripts, URLs, @mentions, #hashtags, digits, and ALL-CAPS acronyms are never flagged.
- **UI**: per-input-event cheap re-check; an "ABC n" badge appears in the composer input row while the draft has misspellings; clicking opens a corrections panel above the composer with up to 5 suggestions per word, **Ignore** (session-only, cleared on send/chat switch) and **Add to dictionary** (persisted to `spellcheck_words.json`). Applying a suggestion replaces the word and restores the cursor after it.
- **Settings**: "Check spelling" toggle in Settings → Appearance (default on, like Telegram Desktop).

## Key decisions

- **No inline wavy underlines**: the kit Textarea is a closed component with no decoration hooks — forking it was rejected as over-engineering. The badge + corrections panel is the full feature without kit surgery.
- **No hunspell/system dictionaries**: nothing ships them on all three OSes; the embedded wordlist is portable.
- Suggestions computed on panel open, never per keystroke.

## Out of scope

Non-English dictionaries (language picker for spellcheck); inline underline rendering if the kit ever supports it.

## Gates

- `cargo fmt` ✓
- `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo test --no-default-features --locked`: **1219 lib + integration tests passed / 0 failed** (incl. 8 spellcheck unit tests) ✓
- Tip-scoped `macos-ui-build`: **not claimed** on this tip (earlier green citation was the wrong SHA; retracted).

## UI proof (Xvfb GPUI captures)

- `docs/screenshots/ready-spellcheck.png` — ABC badge with typos in composer
- `docs/screenshots/ready-spellcheck-panel.png` — corrections panel (capitalized suggestions)
- `docs/screenshots/ready-spellcheck-toggle.png` — Appearance "Check spelling" toggle

## MUST_FIX follow-up

- Toggle OFF immediately clears misspellings / closes panel via `sync_spellcheck`
- `edits1` alphabet includes `'` and `-` (hyphenated dictionary forms reachable)
- Apply + panel suggestions preserve capitalization (`Teh` → `The`)

A real high-contrast theme for the whole app:

- HC as a third `ThemeChoice`, not an orthogonal toggle: the kit `ThemeMode` enum is closed (Light/Dark), and HC supersedes the light/dark choice anyway.
- Did NOT recolor every semantic token: dark-mode semantic values already have good contrast on black.

Incoming bubbles stay very dark gray (0x1a1a1a): bubble text is hardcoded white, so a white HC bubble is impossible without restyling the kit Message component (out of scope).

## Summary

Implements `parity:msg-richtext-ai-tools` — all five TDLib AI composer methods end to end (schema 1.8.67, exact field names).

closedPRs.title: infra: fragment-based parity docs to end README/DECISIONS conflicts
closedPRs.body:
README.md checkbox unions and DECISIONS.md section inserts are the top merge-conflict sources (9 hits in one day across the 4 loops). This PR takes both files out of feature-branch contention entirely.

## New contract

**Coordinators** — feature PRs NEVER touch `README.md` or `DECISIONS.md` (CI fails the PR if you do):
- Declare completed checklist items in `parity-fragments/<slice-id>.txt` (branch name with `/` → `-`), one `parity:<area>-<slug>` ID per line. Only genuinely completed items.
- Write slice specs/decisions/future-work notes to `docs/decisions/<slice-id>.md` (unique filenames can never conflict).

**Reviewers** — verify the declared parity IDs in the fragment are accurate and complete (each one genuinely works in the implementation; nothing completed is missing), instead of verifying checked boxes.

**Merge pipeline** — after a PR merges, you are the ONLY writer of `README.md`:
1. List the fragment files the merge added: `git diff <merge-sha>^1 <merge-sha> --name-only -- parity-fragments/`
2. On a fresh main checkout run `bash scripts/apply-parity-fragment.sh <files>` (flips the boxes, deletes the fragments, idempotent)
3. Commit as `parity: apply #N fragment (k boxes)` and push to main directly.

Parity may lag a merge by a few minutes — acceptable and documented in `parity-fragments/README.md`. `scripts/parity_pct.sh` and the dashboard keep reading `README.md` on main unchanged.

## CI

New `parity-fragments` job in `ci.yml` (PRs only): fails on README/DECISIONS hand-edits, malformed IDs, IDs with no README anchor, and duplicate IDs within the PR. Both scripts were tested against the real README (apply flips boxes idempotently, skips unknown IDs, parity still parses).

## Notes for the pipeline

- The weekly `telegram-update-watch` job keeps its direct-edit right for NEW checklist items (it owns checklist currency); collisions with apply commits are rare — re-run the apply on conflict.
- `DECISIONS.md` stays as the historical archive; new per-slice decisions live in `docs/decisions/`.
- Follow-up for Idan: consider making the `parity-fragments` check a required status.

parity:secret-screenshot-send.evidence: Send mechanism EXISTS in TDLib: viewMessages takes source:MessageSource (td_api.tl:13230) and messageSourceScreenshot exists (td_api.tl:3234) — TGX uses this path. But Linux has no OS screenshot-detection API to trigger it: X11 exposes no screenshot-taken event; Wayland has no standard screenshot-detection protocol; no D-Bus signal from screenshot tools. Independently corroborated by lucid-softworks/react-native-linux Linux screen-capture doc (no portable detection signal; honest no-op). TDLib is UI-agnostic and cannot detect OS screenshots itself. Polling screenshot dirs is flaky (clipboard-only captures, custom paths) — rejected.

parity:secret-screenshot-block.evidence: No FLAG_SECURE equivalent on Linux: X11 any client can XGetImage the root window with no per-window opt-out (protocol fact); Wayland has no standard secure-surface protocol — wp-security-context-v1 is compositor-specific (GNOME mutter partial, sway/others no) and does not reliably block PipeWire/screen-cast capture. td_api.tl grep for secure/prevent/screenshot shows no window-security API (only story protect_content, server-side). TDLib does not do window management. Independently corroborated by the same Linux screen-capture doc (no portable secure-window hint; capture tools succeed regardless).

parity:secret-session-terminate.evidence: td_api.tl 1.8.67: secretChat (line 2816) = id, user_id, state, is_outbound, key_hash, layer — NO session id, NO auth-key linkage. session (line 9144) = capability flags only (can_accept_secret_chats), NO secret-chat linkage. Zero 'auth_key' fields anywhere in td_api.tl. Which auth-key a secret chat is bound to is server-side/internal state not exposed to clients; per-device E2E state means other sessions' secret chats are unknowable client-side anyway. No client-side join key exists, so the count cannot be computed. TGX shows no such count on session termination (its ClosingXSecretChats string is for bulk chat deletion).
